branches.cn: 劳动线：拉丁词根 laborare 让实验室成为干活之地。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: a clipped word travels fast into general speech.
branches.cn: 形式线：截短的词很快走进日常语言。

intro.en: Lab is a clipping; its family is built from the full laboratory and from modern compounds.
intro.cn: lab 是截短词，其词族由完整的 laboratory 与现代合成构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin work root behind laboratory is recorded in labor and laborare.
latinIntro.cn: laboratory 背后的拉丁语「劳动」词根在 labor 与 laborare 中都有记录。

items.example: The new labs open in May.
The laboratory is on floor two.
It forms laboratory and factory-like words.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 laboratory 一类表示场所的词。

items.example: He put on a clean lab coat.
The language lab has forty seats.

items.meaningCN: 构成 lab work（实验工作）
items.example: Lab work counts for half the mark.

definition_zh: 标签；标记；称号；贴标签；把……称为
definition_en: a small piece of paper or cloth giving information about something, a word used to describe a person or group, or to fix such a tag on something
core_image: 一只玻璃罐上贴着一方白纸，写着内容与日期
scene: 厨房的架子上摆满一排玻璃罐，里面装着不同颜色的粉。She wrote the date on a label and stuck it to the jar of flour.
sceneCN: 这里 label 是「标签」（第 1 个义项：提供信息的小纸片或布片），句意是她在标签上写了日期，贴在面粉罐上。画面里有厨房架子、一排玻璃罐与一方白纸。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ed 构成，义为「贴有标签的；被称作的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「贴标签；标签说明」
植物学术语，由本词派生，义为「有唇瓣的」

senses.title: A tag giving information
senses.definition: a small piece of paper, cloth, or plastic fixed to an object to show what it is, who made it, or what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 贴在物件上、说明其名称、制作者或成分的小纸片、布片或塑片
senses.example: The washing label says to use cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 洗标上写着要用冷水洗。
senses.why: The core object is a small carrier of written information attached to something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是一小块信息的载体，附着在更大的物体上。

senses.title: A word used to classify someone
senses.definition: a short word or phrase used to describe a person, a group, or a style, often too simply
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述某人、某群体或某种风格的简短词语，常失之简单
senses.example: She dislikes the label of a protest singer.
senses.exampleCN: 她不喜欢「抗议歌手」这个标签。
senses.why: Once the written tag is put on an object, the same gesture is done to people with a word, and the metaphor is fixed.
senses.whyCN: 文字标签既可贴物，同样的动作也可以用词贴人，这个比喻便固定下来。

senses.title: To fix a tag on something
senses.definition: to attach a label to an object, or to write information on it
senses.definitionCN: 给物件贴标签，或在上面写明信息
senses.example: All the boxes must be labelled before shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 所有箱子在发运前都必须贴好标签。
senses.why: The noun of a tag becomes the verb of attaching one, as English commonly does with objects.
senses.whyCN: 标签这一物件名词转为「贴上标签」的动词，英语中这类器物转动词很常见。

senses.title: To describe or brand
senses.definition: to describe a person or thing with a particular word, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 用某个词描述某人或某物，常带不公意味
senses.example: The paper labelled the plan a waste of money.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把这项计划称作浪费钱。
senses.why: The verb repeats on people what the noun does to jars: a word is stuck on and then treated as the truth.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词对罐子所做的事用到人身上：把一个词贴上去，随后当作事实。

senses.title: A brand name on goods
senses.definition: the name of a company or designer shown on a product, especially in fashion
senses.definitionCN: 商品上显示的公司或设计师名称，尤见于时装
senses.example: He refuses to pay extra for a designer label.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝为名牌标识多付钱。
senses.why: In fashion the maker name became the thing itself, so a label on the collar can double the price.
senses.whyCN: 在时装业里制作者之名成了东西本身，于是领口上一个标签就能让价格翻倍。

intro.en: Label comes from an Old French word for a rag or ribbon, and its meaning moved from the strip to the information written on it.
intro.cn: label 源自古法语中表示「布条、丝带」的词，词义由那条带子转到写在带子上的信息。

items.en: A Germanic root meaning to hang down or to flap lies behind the French word.
items.cn: 法语这个词的背后，是一个表示「垂下、飘动」的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Label meant a narrow strip or ribbon hanging loose, often attached to a seal or a garment.
items.cn: label 指垂着的一条窄带或丝带，常系在印章或衣物上。

items.en: English borrowed it for the paper strip that carried a name or an address.
items.cn: 英语借它指写着名字或地址的纸条。

items.en: The strip and its writing merged, so label came to mean the written information itself.
items.cn: 带子与上面的文字合为一体，label 遂指文字信息本身。

items.en: The word turns into a metaphor and a verb: people are labelled, and brands are labels.
items.cn: 这个词转为比喻与动词：人被贴标签，品牌也被称作 label。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derived forms and close spellings; the near-meaning group gathers other words for tags and names.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与相近拼写；近义组收其他表示标签与名称的词。

entries.definition: The past form and adjective, spelled with one l in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式与形容词，美式英语只写一个 l。

entries.definition: A common wrong spelling, with the two letters swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 常见错拼，两个字母颠倒了。

entries.definition: One letter away, and it means a published false statement that harms someone.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指发表出来损害他人的不实之词。

entries.definition: A small movable card or plastic piece attached to show price or owner.
entries.definitionCN: 附于物件、显示价格或主人的可移动小牌。

entries.definition: A gummed piece of paper stuck on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 贴在表面的带胶纸片。

entries.definition: The name of a product or company, or a mark made by burning.
entries.definitionCN: 产品或公司的名称，也可指烙印。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the rag origin of the word, the British and American spellings, and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用这个词「布条」的来源、英美两种拼写，以及常见搭配。

normal.en: Label once meant a hanging strip of cloth, and now it means what is written on it.
normal.cn: label 原是垂着的一条布，如今指写在布上的字。

normal.en: British English doubles the l: labelled, labelling.
normal.cn: 英式英语双写 l：labelled、labelling。

normal.en: Read the label before you wash the shirt.
normal.cn: 洗衬衫之前先看标签。

normal.en: To label someone is to stick a word on them and walk away.
normal.cn: 给某人贴标签，就是把一个词贴在他身上然后走开。

normal.en: A designer label costs more for the name than for the cloth.
normal.cn: 名牌标识贵的是名字，而非布料。

abstract.en: A label is a promise of order: one small paper, and a whole shelf becomes readable.
abstract.cn: 标签是秩序的一份承诺：一小片纸，整排架子便读得懂。

abstract.en: The same act that helps a jar be found can make a person be misunderstood.
abstract.cn: 帮人找到罐子的同一动作，也能让人被误解。

abstract.en: What is written on the outside is not the thing inside, a difference worth keeping in mind whenever a label is read.
abstract.cn: 外面写的并非里面之物，每次看标签时都值得记住这个差别。

examples.en: Check the label for the ingredients.
examples.cn: 查看标签上的成分表。

examples.en: Every file was labelled with a date.
examples.cn: 每个文件都标上了日期。

examples.en: It is unfair to label him a trouble-maker.
examples.cn: 称他为麻烦制造者是不公平的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累抱」——抱着罐子累了一路，就为看清那方标签

root: 古法语 label「垂着的布条、丝带」，背后是表示「垂下」的日耳曼语词根；中古英语借入指写有姓名地址的纸条，后由带子转为上面所写的信息，并引申出「称号」与「贴标签、把……称为」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the information tag, the word used of a person, the act of tagging, the act of branding someone with a word, and the brand name on goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：信息标签，用于人的称号，贴标签的动作，用词给人定性，以及商品上的品牌标识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square of white paper on a jar, with a name and a date in ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃罐上一方白纸，墨写着名称与日期。

branches.en: THE TAG LINE: a small carrier of written information attached to a thing.
branches.cn: 标签线：附着在物件上、承载文字信息的小片。

branches.en: THE WORD LINE: a short word stuck on a person, a style or a garment.
branches.cn: 词语线：贴在人、风格或衣物上的简短说法。

branches.en: THE ACTION LINE: the verb fixes a tag on an object.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词给物件贴上标签。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT LINE: the same act with words can be unfair.
branches.cn: 判断线：用词做同样的事，可能不公。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: object and action share one form, as English often allows.
branches.cn: 形式线：物件与动作共用一个形式，英语常这样。

intro.en: Label is a French loan whose family grows through spelling variants and ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: label 是法语借词，其词族靠拼写变体与普通后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Label is not Latin in origin, though the French form goes back to a Germanic strip.
latinIntro.cn: label 并非源自拉丁语，其法语形式可上溯到日耳曼语中「布条」一词。

definition_zh: 实验室；实验楼；研究室；实验课
definition_en: a room or building equipped for scientific experiments, research, and testing, or the work carried on in it
core_image: 一整层楼里都摆着长台，仪器在灯下泛出冷光
scene: 实验楼的门牌是不锈钢的，走廊里能听到通风柜低低的嗡声。The whole laboratory was working on a single problem that winter.
sceneCN: 这里 laboratory 是「实验室」（第 1 个义项：配备设备进行科学实验与研究的场所），句意是那个冬天整个实验室都在攻克同一个问题。画面里有不锈钢门牌、走廊与通风柜的嗡声。

pos.zh: 名词：实验室；实验室工作；研究室

derivatives.zh: laboratory 的缩略形式，义为「实验室」
由本词派生，义为「实验室工作人员」
由本词派生，义为「实验室的」

senses.title: A room equipped for experiments
senses.definition: a room fitted with instruments and apparatus for scientific experiments and tests
senses.definitionCN: 配有仪器设备、用于科学实验与检测的房间
senses.example: The laboratory was closed while the equipment was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 设备更换期间实验室关闭了。
senses.why: The word names a place built for work, and in science that work is experiment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指为工作而建的场所，在科学里那项工作就是实验。

senses.title: A building or department for research
senses.definition: a whole building or a research unit where scientific work is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 开展科学工作的整栋建筑或一个研究单位
senses.example: He has worked at the national laboratory for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在国家实验室工作了二十年。
senses.why: One equipped room became the seed of a whole institution, so the place name grew to a building or a research unit.
senses.whyCN: 一间配好设备的房间成了一整个机构的种子，于是这个词从房间扩大到建筑或研究单位。

senses.title: The work done there
senses.definition: the practical scientific work itself, often in phrases such as laboratory practice
senses.definitionCN: 实验工作本身，常见于 laboratory practice 一类说法
senses.example: Good laboratory practice keeps results reliable.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的实验操作规范让结果可靠。
senses.why: The place names its own activity, the way a school can stand for schooling.
senses.whyCN: 场所为其自身的活动命名，正如学校可以代表教育本身。

intro.en: Laboratory is a Medieval Latin place noun from the verb to work, and it was used in alchemy before it reached science.
intro.cn: laboratory 是源自「工作」动词的中世纪拉丁语场所名词，先用于炼金术，后进入科学。

items.en: The verb laborare meant to work or toil, and labor meant toil itself.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为「工作、劳作」，labor 即劳累本身。

items.en: Laboratorium named a place for work, and alchemists used it for rooms of furnaces and stills.
items.cn: laboratorium 指工作之所，炼金术士用它称呼摆满炉与蒸馏器的房间。

items.en: English borrows laboratory in the seventeenth century for rooms of chemical and physical work.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 laboratory，指做化学与物理工作的房间。

items.en: British speech shortens it to lab, and American use puts the stress on the first syllable.
items.cn: 英式口语把它缩为 lab，美式则把重音放在第一音节。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spreads from chemistry to psychology, language study and industry.
items.cn: 二十世纪里这个词从化学扩展到心理学、语言教学与工业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin work root and forms of this word; the near-meaning group gathers other places of study and work.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「劳动」词根的词与本词的形式；近义组收其他学习与工作场所。

entries.definition: The everyday clipping of laboratory.
entries.definitionCN: laboratory 的日常缩略形式。

entries.definition: The Latin work root in its other English form, meaning toil or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁语词根的另一英语形式，指劳作或劳工。

entries.definition: Built on the same work root, meaning worked out in great detail.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该词根，义为「精心制作的」。

entries.definition: A room with tools for making, not for controlled experiment.
entries.definitionCN: 放工具做制作的房间，不是做受控实验的。

entries.definition: A place built to watch the sky, named after looking rather than working.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的地方，以「看」而非「做」命名。

entries.definition: An organisation for research or teaching, larger than one room.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或教学机构，规模大于一个房间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the British and American stress, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语词根、英美重音差别，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Laboratory is built on laborare, to work, so it is a room for work.
normal.cn: laboratory 建立在 laborare（工作）之上，所以是为了干活而设的屋子。

normal.en: Alchemists had laboratories before scientists did.
normal.cn: 炼金术士比科学家更早拥有实验室。

normal.en: British speakers say it with four beats, American speakers with three.
normal.cn: 英式读音是四个音节，美式是三个。

normal.en: Laboratory equipment and laboratory test are the standard pairings.
normal.cn: laboratory equipment 与 laboratory test 是标准搭配。

normal.en: The lab is the same word with the middle taken out.
normal.cn: lab 就是这个词挖掉中间的那一截。

abstract.en: A laboratory is a place where the world is made small enough to question.
abstract.cn: 实验室是把世界缩小到可以被追问的地方。

abstract.en: The name means only workroom, yet the work inside keeps turning guesses into evidence.
abstract.cn: 它的名字只意味着「工作间」，里面的事却不断把猜测变成证据。

abstract.en: Any place built to test a claim, from a clinic to a city, now borrows this name.
abstract.cn: 任何为检验主张而建的地方，从诊所到城市，如今都借用这个名字。

examples.en: The samples are analysed in a licensed laboratory.
examples.cn: 样本在具备资质的实验室里分析。

examples.en: The laboratory moved into a larger building last year.
examples.cn: 这个实验室去年搬进了更大的楼里。

examples.en: Laboratory work takes a third of the course.
examples.cn: 实验工作占这门课程的三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: labor 劳动 + -atory 场所——干活的地方，就是实验室

root: 拉丁语 laborare（工作、劳作）派生名词 laboratorium（干活之所），中世纪拉丁语中用于炼金术的工作室；十七世纪英语借入，指科学实验场所，后缩略为 lab，并扩展至心理学、语言教学与工业研究。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the equipped room, the building or research unit it grew into, and the practical work carried on there.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：配备仪器的房间，由它扩展而成的整栋建筑或研究单位，以及在那里进行的实验工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: long benches under cold lights, instruments waiting to be used.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷白灯光下的长台，仪器等着被使用。

branches.en: THE ROOM LINE: a space fitted with apparatus for tests.
branches.cn: 房间线：为检测而装设仪器的空间。

branches.en: THE BUILDING LINE: the name grows to a whole research unit.
branches.cn: 建筑线：名字可扩展到整个研究单位。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY LINE: the place stands for the work done in it.
branches.cn: 活动线：场所代表在其中所做的工作。

branches.en: THE ROOT LINE: laborare makes the word a workroom by origin.
branches.cn: 词根线：laborare 让这个词在原义上就是工作间。

branches.en: THE SHORT LINE: the clipping lab is now the everyday form.
branches.cn: 简短线：缩略形式 lab 已成日常说法。

intro.en: Laboratory is a Latin place noun whose family in English is mainly the clipping, plus a few formal derivatives.
intro.cn: laboratory 是拉丁语场所名词，其英语词族主要是截短形式与少数正式派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor, laborare, laboratorium and elaborare are all recorded, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 labor、laborare、laboratorium 与 elaborare 均有记录，故此无构拟成分。

items.example: The laboratory is quiet at night.
The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整族的源头。

items.example: It marks a laboratory for research.
items.exampleCN: 它标明用于研究的实验室。

latinEntries.meaning: to work out, to take pains

definition_zh: 劳动；工作；劳动力；工党；分娩
definition_en: physical or mental work, especially hard work; also the workforce as a group and the process of giving birth
core_image: 两只手紧握工具，把力气一点点变成看得见的成果
scene: 天还没亮，工地上的灯已经亮起，工人们把沉重的沙袋一袋袋扛上肩。After a long day of labour, the crew sat down beside the unfinished wall.
sceneCN: 这里是「劳动、劳作」（第 1 个义项：付出体力的工作）；句意为干了一整天活之后，工人们坐在未完工的墙边歇下。图中可辨识物件：工地灯、沙袋、半截砖墙。

derivatives.zh: 由 labour 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「劳动者；工人」
由拉丁词干 labor 加 -ious 构成，义为「费力的；艰苦的」
由 labour 与 intensive 复合而成，义为「劳动密集型的」

senses.title: Physical work, especially of a hard kind
senses.definition: work, especially hard physical work, done with effort over time
senses.definitionCN: 尤指需要长时间付出体力的艰苦工作
senses.example: The wall was built through months of hard labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙是经过数月苦干才砌成的。
senses.why: Latin labor meant toil and hardship, so the word starts from the strain felt in the body rather than from the finished product.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 labor 本义是「辛劳、艰苦」，所以这个词的起点是身体感到的吃力，而不是最后完成的成果。

senses.title: The workforce as a group
senses.definition: the people who work, considered as a whole, especially in an industry or country
senses.definitionCN: 把从事工作的人作为一个整体来看，尤指某一行业或国家的劳动力
senses.example: The factory needs more skilled labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂需要更多技术工人。
senses.why: Once labour names the effort, it can also name the people who supply that effort, which is why the word shifts from activity to a collective body.
senses.whyCN: 既然 labour 能指付出的力气，也就能指提供这些力气的人，于是词义从「活动」转到「集体的人群」。

senses.title: Organized political labour
senses.titleCN: 工党；有组织的劳工运动
senses.definition: the political party or movement that represents the interests of workers
senses.definitionCN: 代表工人利益的政治党派或有组织的运动
senses.example: He voted for Labour in the last election.
senses.exampleCN: 上次选举他投了工党的票。
senses.why: When workers organize, the same word moves from the shop floor to the ballot box, naming the political force built on their shared interests.
senses.whyCN: 当工人联合起来，同一个词就从车间走向投票箱，用来指建立在他们共同利益之上的政治力量。

senses.title: Childbirth
senses.definition: the process of giving birth, especially the final stage with strong contractions
senses.definitionCN: 生育的过程，尤指伴随强烈宫缩的最后阶段
senses.example: She went into labour at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黎明时开始分娩。
senses.why: Childbirth is the hardest bodily work a person can do, so English borrowed the word for toil to describe it, keeping the sense of intense physical effort.
senses.whyCN: 分娩是人身体上最吃力的一种劳作，英语便借「辛苦出力」这个词来描述它，保留了强烈体力付出的意味。

intro.en: Labour is a Latin word for toil that travelled through French before it named work, workers and birth in English.
intro.cn: labour 是拉丁语中表示「辛劳」的词，经法语进入英语，先指干活，再指劳动者与分娩。

items.en: Labor meant toil, hardship and effort, and it could also name the fruit of that effort.
items.cn: labor 意为辛劳、艰苦、出力，也可指付出之后得到的成果。

items.en: The verb laborare meant to work or to struggle, and it supplied the family of words about effort.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为干活、挣扎，派生出一整族与出力有关的词。

items.en: Old French took the noun as labour, meaning work or task, and passed it to English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 labour，意为工作、活儿，诺曼征服之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English labour covered both the act of working and the trouble or hardship that came with it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 labour 同时指干活这件事和随之而来的辛苦、磨难。

items.en: Modern English keeps the British spelling labour and the American labor, and extends the word to workers, their party and childbirth.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式 labour 与美式 labor 两种拼写，并把词义扩展到劳动者、工党与分娩。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects words for work and effort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示工作与出力的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of labour, with the same meanings.
entries.definitionCN: labour 的美式拼写，含义完全相同。

entries.definition: Needing a lot of time and effort to do.
entries.definitionCN: 需要花费大量时间与力气的；费力的。

entries.definition: A room or building used for scientific work.
entries.definitionCN: 用于科学工作的房间或建筑；实验室。

entries.definition: To work together with someone on a task.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人合作完成一项任务。

entries.definition: Activity done to achieve a purpose, often as a job.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而从事的活动，常指工作。

entries.definition: Long, hard and tiring work.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间、艰苦而累人的劳动。

entries.definition: The energy spent trying to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 为做某事而付出的精力。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for toil, and its family keeps returning to effort, hardship and the people who do the work.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「辛劳」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到出力、艰苦以及干活的人。

normal.en: Labor in Latin means toil, so labour is not just work but work that costs the body something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 labor 意为辛劳，所以 labour 不只是工作，而是让身体付出代价的活。

normal.en: Labourer adds -er to labour: the person who does the labour.
normal.cn: labourer 在 labour 后加 -er，就是「干活的人」。

normal.en: Laborious adds -ious to the same stem: full of labour, therefore tiring.
normal.cn: laborious 在同一词干后加 -ious，意为「充满劳作的」，因此是费力的。

normal.en: The British spelling has a u, the American spelling drops it, just like colour and color.
normal.cn: 英式拼写带 u，美式去掉 u，就像 colour 与 color 一样。

normal.en: Labour Party is capitalized because it names a political party, not work in general.
normal.cn: Labour Party 首字母大写，因为它指一个政党，而不是泛指劳动。

abstract.en: A single word for effort, workers and birth suggests that English treats all three as kinds of hard work.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示出力、劳动者和分娩，说明英语把这三者都看成某种辛苦的劳作。

abstract.en: When a word moves from the body to the ballot box, the same strain is being organized into power.
abstract.cn: 当一个词从身体走向投票箱，同样的辛苦被组织成了力量。

abstract.en: Labour is a reminder that behind every finished thing there is a stretch of time that somebody had to endure.
abstract.cn: labour 提醒人：每件完成的东西背后，都有一段有人必须熬过去的时间。

examples.en: The wall was built through months of hard labour.
examples.cn: 这堵墙是经过数月苦干才砌成的。

examples.en: The country's labour force is growing older.
examples.cn: 这个国家的劳动力正在老龄化。

examples.en: She was in labour for six hours.
examples.cn: 她分娩持续了六个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累吧」——活儿干多了，人就会喊着累吧；记住 labour 是劳动。

root: 拉丁语 labor（劳作、辛苦）经古法语 labour 进入英语；同族词多与「干活、费力气」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is effortful work; the senses then divide into the people who work, their political party, and the hardest bodily work of all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是费力的工作；义项由此分出干活的人、代表他们的政党，以及最吃力的身体劳作——分娩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a tool and turning effort into a visible result.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手紧握工具，把力气一点点变成看得见的成果。

branches.en: a wall rising slowly under a hot sun
branches.cn: 烈日下一寸寸升起的墙

branches.en: a worker counting the hours until the shift ends
branches.cn: 工人数着还有多久下工

branches.en: a factory hiring more hands for the season
branches.cn: 工厂为旺季多招人手

branches.en: a ballot box standing in for the shop floor
branches.cn: 投票箱代替了车间

branches.en: a family waiting outside a delivery room
branches.cn: 产房外等候的一家人

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun of toil, its verb, and two English suffixes that turn it into a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示辛劳的拉丁名词、它的动词，以及两个把它变成「人」和「性质」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 缺乏；不足；缺少
definition_en: the state of not having something, or to be without something that is needed
core_image: 一只空碗摆在桌上，该有的东西一样也没盛上
scene: 厨房的储物柜被拉开，里面只剩几个空罐子。The cake failed because of a lack of flour.
sceneCN: 这里是「缺少、不足」（第 1 个义项：名词，指某物不存在或数量不够）；句意为蛋糕因为面粉不够而做失败了。图中可辨识物件：空罐子、空碗、打开的橱柜。

derivatives.zh: 由 lack 加 -ing 构成，义为「缺少的；不足的」
由 lack 与 luster（光泽）复合而成，义为「暗淡的；平淡无奇的」

senses.title: The state of not having enough of something
senses.definition: the state of not having something, or of not having enough of it
senses.definitionCN: 某物不存在或数量不够的状态
senses.example: The project was delayed by a lack of funds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目因为资金不足而推迟。
senses.why: Lack names an empty place where something should be; the word points at the gap rather than at any object.
senses.whyCN: lack 指的是本该有东西却空着的位置，它指向的是那个缺口，而不是任何具体物件。

senses.title: To be without something needed
senses.definition: to have none of something, or not enough of it
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有某物，或某物的量不够
senses.example: Many students lack confidence in speaking English.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生说英语时缺乏信心。
senses.why: The noun was turned into a verb without adding a suffix, so 'to lack' is simply to be in the state the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词原样转成动词，没有加后缀，所以 to lack 就是处在名词所指的那种「空着」的状态。

senses.title: A shortage that causes trouble
senses.definition: a shortage of something necessary, especially one that causes difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 必要之物短缺，尤指因此造成困难的情形
senses.example: The old town suffers from a lack of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城饱受清洁水源短缺之苦。
senses.why: When the missing thing is necessary, the gap becomes a problem, and English extends lack from a neutral absence to a damaging shortage.
senses.whyCN: 当缺的是必需品时，那个缺口就成了麻烦，英语便从「中性的没有」扩展到「有害的短缺」。

intro.en: Lack is a Middle English word for a gap or deficiency, and its earlier source is not fully settled.
intro.cn: lack 是中古英语中表示「缺口、不足」的词，更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Lak meant a deficiency, fault or want, and it was used both as a noun and as a verb.
items.cn: lak 意为不足、缺陷、匮乏，名词与动词两种用法都有。

items.en: Many dictionaries suggest a Middle Dutch or Middle Low German source with the same sense, but the path is uncertain.
items.cn: 多数词典推测它来自意义相同的中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，但具体路径并不确定。

items.en: The word is recorded in English from the twelfth century onward, always close to the idea of something missing.
items.cn: 这个词从十二世纪起见于英语文献，始终贴近「有东西缺失」的概念。

items.en: Early modern writers use lack for both material shortage and personal fault, widening its range.
items.cn: 近代早期作家用 lack 兼指物资短缺与人的缺点，词义范围随之扩大。

items.en: Modern English keeps the simple noun and verb and builds phrases such as for lack of and lack of sleep.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词与动词的基本用法，并形成 for lack of、lack of sleep 等搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the spelling or the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for absence and shortage.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同词干的词；近义组收表示「没有、短缺」的词。

entries.definition: Missing or not having enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少的；不足的。

entries.definition: Dull and without energy or brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 暗淡的；平淡无奇的。

entries.definition: A servant who obeys orders without question.
entries.definitionCN: 唯命是从的仆人；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To fall behind or a delay.
entries.definitionCN: 落后；滞后；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 短缺；不足。

entries.definition: The state of something not being present.
entries.definitionCN: 缺席；不存在。

entries.definition: A lack of something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏；需要。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and blunt, and its few relatives all circle the idea of an empty place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短促直接，少数同族词都围绕「空着的位置」这一意思。

normal.en: Lack is both noun and verb with no change of shape: a lack of water, to lack water.
normal.cn: lack 名动同形：a lack of water 与 to lack water 都不加后缀。

normal.en: For lack of is a fixed phrase meaning 'because something is missing'.
normal.cn: for lack of 是固定搭配，意为「因为缺少某物」。

normal.en: Lacking adds -ing and works as an adjective: the lacking supplies.
normal.cn: lacking 加 -ing 作形容词：缺少的物资。

normal.en: Lackluster joins lack to luster, a word for shine.
normal.cn: lackluster 把 lack 与表示光泽的 luster 组合起来。

normal.en: The word never takes an article before the missing thing: lack of time, not lack of the time.
normal.cn: 说 lack of time，不说 lack of the time。

abstract.en: A word for a hole in a set of things reminds us that language can point at what is not there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「一套东西里的空洞」的词，提醒人语言也能指向不在场的东西。

abstract.en: Because lack is neutral in shape, only context tells whether the gap is mild or dangerous.
abstract.cn: lack 本身是中性的，只有上下文才说明这个缺口是轻微还是危险。

abstract.en: Every shortage is measured against a standard that says how much should have been there.
abstract.cn: 每一种短缺都是对照「本该有多少」的标准量出来的。

examples.en: The cake failed because of a lack of flour.
examples.cn: 蛋糕因为面粉不够而做失败了。

examples.en: Many students lack confidence in speaking English.
examples.cn: 许多学生说英语时缺乏信心。

examples.en: There is no lack of volunteers for the event.
examples.cn: 这项活动的志愿者并不缺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克」——东西没来够克数，就是缺；lack 记作「缺」。

root: 中古英语 lak（不足、缺陷），更早来源一般推测为中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，具体路径来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an empty place where something should be; the senses move from a neutral absence to a verb and then to a harmful shortage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「本该有东西的空位」；义项从「中性的没有」转到动词用法，再转到「有害的短缺」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl on a table where food should have been.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摆着一只空碗，本该盛着食物。

branches.en: a pantry shelf with nothing on it
branches.cn: 空空如也的食品架

branches.en: a speaker searching for a word that will not come
branches.cn: 说话人找不到合适的词

branches.en: a village waiting for a water truck
branches.cn: 等水车来的村子

branches.en: the same gap, first seen and then suffered
branches.cn: 同一个缺口，先被看见，再让人吃苦

branches.en: a hand reaching for a tool that is not there
branches.cn: 伸手去拿却不存在的工具

intro.en: The word is a bare English stem with two common suffixes and one compound in its family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个光裸的英语词干，同族里有两个常见后缀和一个复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的 -ing 后缀
构成过去式的 -ed 后缀

definition_zh: 落后；滞后；时间间隔
definition_en: to fall behind others in movement or progress, or a delay between two events
core_image: 队伍前面的人已转过弯，最后一个还在原地系鞋带
scene: 操场上的队伍已经跑出半圈，最后一名选手才刚系好鞋带。The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
sceneCN: 这里是「落后、跟不上」（第 1 个义项：动词，指行动或进度落在别人后面）；句意为最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。图中可辨识物件：跑道、系鞋带的选手、远处的队伍。

derivatives.zh: 由 lag 双写 g 加 -ing 构成，义为「落后的；滞后」
由 lag 加 -ard 构成，义为「迟缓的人；落后者」

senses.title: To fall behind in movement or progress
senses.definition: to move or develop more slowly than others, so that a distance opens up
senses.definitionCN: 行动或发展比其他人慢，因而拉开距离
senses.example: The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
senses.exampleCN: 最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。
senses.why: Lag probably imitates the sense of something dragging at the back; the word pictures a trailing end rather than a measured distance.
senses.whyCN: lag 很可能来自「拖在后面」的感觉，它描绘的是队尾，而不是量出来的距离。

senses.title: A delay between two connected events
senses.definition: the period of time by which one event follows another that should be simultaneous
senses.definitionCN: 两个本应同时的事件之间相隔的那段时间
senses.example: There is a slight time lag between the sound and the picture.
senses.exampleCN: 声音和画面之间有一点时间滞后。
senses.why: Once the verb names being behind, the noun can name the measurable gap itself, as in a time lag.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示「落在后面」，名词就能指那段可测量的差距，例如 time lag。

senses.title: The tiredness caused by crossing time zones
senses.definition: the bodily discomfort felt after a long flight across several time zones
senses.definitionCN: 跨越多个时区长途飞行后身体感到的不适
senses.example: It took him three days to get over his jet lag.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了三天才缓过时差反应。
senses.why: The body's internal clock lags behind local time after a flight, and the compound jet lag names exactly that lag.
senses.whyCN: 飞行之后，身体的生物钟落后于当地时间，jet lag 这个复合词正是把这种「滞后」说了出来。

intro.en: Lag is a word of uncertain origin, usually connected with Scandinavian forms for something dragging behind.
intro.cn: lag 来源不确定，通常与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「拖在后面」的形式相联系。

items.en: The earliest records do not settle whether lag came from Scandinavian or from an English dialect.
items.cn: 最早记录无法确定 lag 是来自斯堪的纳维亚语还是英格兰方言。

items.en: A related Swedish dialect verb for moving slowly or dragging is often cited, but the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 常被提到的是一个意义为「慢慢移动、拖」的瑞典方言动词，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Lag appears in English in the sixteenth century with the sense of trailing behind.
items.cn: lag 在十六世纪进入英语，意为「拖在后面」。

items.en: The noun and the modern technical sense of a time lag develop in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词用法以及 time lag 这一现代技术义在十九世纪发展出来。

items.en: Modern English adds jet lag and digital lag, keeping the same picture of something running behind.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上 jet lag 与 digital lag，仍保留「某物跑在后面」的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that resemble lag in spelling; the near-meaning group collects words for delay and trailing behind.
note.cn: 形近组收与 lag 拼写相近的词；近义组收表示延迟、落后的词。

entries.definition: A piece of cloth used as a signal, or to become tired.
entries.definitionCN: 旗子；也可指「变得疲倦」；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A small label attached to something.
entries.definitionCN: 标签；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: Falling behind, or material used for insulation.
entries.definitionCN: 落后的；保温材料。

entries.definition: A period of waiting before something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 延迟；耽搁。

entries.definition: To be behind others in a race or competition.
entries.definitionCN: 落后；尾随。

entries.definition: A reduction in speed or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 减速；放慢。

normalIntro.en: The word is short, with a doubled g in its inflections, and its family stays close to the trailing end of a line.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，变形时双写 g，同族词都贴近队伍末尾。

normal.en: Lag doubles its g before -ed and -ing: lagged, lagging.
normal.cn: lag 在 -ed、-ing 前双写 g：lagged、lagging。

normal.en: Lag behind is the common phrase for being slower than others.
normal.cn: lag behind 是表示「落在别人后面」的常用搭配。

normal.en: Time lag is the measurable gap between two events.
normal.cn: time lag 是两个事件之间可测量的间隔。

normal.en: Jet lag joins jet to lag for the tiredness after a flight.
normal.cn: jet lag 把 jet 与 lag 组合，指飞行后的疲倦。

normal.en: Laggard adds -ard, a suffix seen in words for people with a habit.
normal.cn: laggard 加 -ard，这个后缀常见于表示有某种习性的人。

abstract.en: A trailing end is not a fixed distance but a relation: someone must be ahead for lag to exist.
abstract.cn: 队尾不是固定距离而是一种关系：必须有人在前面，才有 lag。

abstract.en: The same word covers a runner, a machine and a body clock, because all three can run behind an expected pace.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指跑步的人、机器和生物钟，因为三者都可能落后于预期节奏。

abstract.en: Lag turns difference in speed into something you can name and measure.
abstract.cn: lag 把速度上的差异变成可以命名、可以测量的东西。

examples.en: The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
examples.cn: 最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。

examples.en: There is a slight time lag between the sound and the picture.
examples.cn: 声音和画面之间有一点时间滞后。

examples.en: It took him three days to get over his jet lag.
examples.cn: 他花了三天才缓过时差反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖格」——赖在格子里不肯往前走，就落后了；lag 记作「落后」。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「拖在后面」的方言动词有关，确切形式无法确认。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a trailing end; it extends from a person falling behind to a measurable time gap and to the body clock running late.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拖在队尾」；由人落后扩展到可测量的时间差，再扩展到生物钟的错后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last runner still tying a shoelace while the line turns the corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：队伍已经转过弯，最后一名还在系鞋带。

branches.en: a runner at the back of the pack
branches.cn: 跑在队伍最后的人

branches.en: a clock that is a few seconds slow
branches.cn: 慢了几秒的钟

branches.en: a traveller awake at the wrong hour
branches.cn: 在错误时间醒来的旅客

branches.en: the same backward pull, in legs and in seconds
branches.cn: 同一种向后拖的力量，表现在腿上和秒数上

branches.en: two screens showing the same scene a beat apart
branches.cn: 两块屏幕同一画面差了一拍

intro.en: There is no settled prefix or root here, so the family is built from the bare stem and two suffixes.
intro.cn: 这里没有确定的前缀或词根，同族词由光裸词干加两个后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 陆地；土地；国土；登陆；着陆
definition_en: the solid surface of the earth, ground or a country, or to come down onto the ground
core_image: 船头前方浮出一条灰绿色的海岸线，脚下的甲板终于能换成泥土
scene: 飞机穿过云层，跑道在下方一点点变大。The plane landed safely on the runway.
sceneCN: 这里是「着陆、降落」（第 4 个义项：动词，指飞行器触地停下）；句意为飞机安全地降落在跑道上。图中可辨识物件：云层、跑道、正在下降的飞机。

derivatives.zh: 由 land 加 -ing 构成，义为「着陆；登陆；楼梯平台」
由 land 与 -scape（景色）复合，义为「风景；景观」

senses.title: The solid surface of the earth
senses.definition: the part of the earth's surface that is not covered by water
senses.definitionCN: 地球表面没有被水覆盖的部分
senses.example: After weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
senses.exampleCN: 在海上漂了几周之后，水手们终于看见了陆地。
senses.why: Land begins as the dry ground that a boat can reach, a boundary between water and solid earth.
senses.whyCN: land 最初指船只能抵达的干燥地面，是水与坚实大地之间的分界。

senses.title: Ground used for a purpose
senses.definition: ground owned or used by someone, especially for farming or building
senses.definitionCN: 某人拥有或使用的土地，尤指用于耕种或建造
senses.example: The family has farmed this land for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人在这块土地上耕种了三代。
senses.why: Once land means solid ground, it can be divided, owned and worked, so the word comes to mean a piece of ground with a use.
senses.whyCN: 既然 land 指坚实的地面，就可以被划分、拥有和耕作，于是它转而指一块有用途的地。

senses.title: A country or nation
senses.definition: a country, especially one thought of as the home of a people
senses.definitionCN: 国家，尤指被视为一个民族家园的国土
senses.example: She returned to her native land after many years abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外多年之后，她回到了故土。
senses.why: A people's ground is their country, so land shifts from soil to the political and emotional idea of a homeland.
senses.whyCN: 一个民族脚下的土地就是他们的国家，于是 land 从泥土转到「故土」这一政治与情感概念。

senses.title: To come down to the ground
senses.definition: to come to the ground from the air or from water, especially after a flight
senses.definitionCN: 从空中或水上来到地面，尤指飞行之后
senses.example: The plane landed safely on the runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机安全地降落在跑道上。
senses.why: The noun names the ground; the verb reverses the direction and means reaching that ground, as a plane or a boat does.
senses.whyCN: 名词指地面；动词把方向反过来，表示抵达地面，飞机或船就是这样。

senses.title: To succeed in getting something
senses.definition: to succeed in obtaining a job, a contract or an opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 成功得到工作、合同或机会
senses.example: He landed a good job at a design studio.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一家设计工作室找到了一份好工作。
senses.why: To land a job is to bring something down and secure it, like a plane touching the ground after a search.
senses.whyCN: land a job 就像飞机经过搜寻后触地一样，把某样东西稳稳弄到手。

intro.en: Land is an Old English word shared across the Germanic languages, with a deep but partly reconstructed root.
intro.cn: land 是古英语词，在日耳曼语族中广泛共享，其更深词根有一部分属于重构形式。

items.en: Land meant earth, territory or a country, and it already carried both the physical and the political sense.
items.cn: land 意为土地、领土或国家，已经同时带有自然与政治两层意思。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form *landa is shared by German Land and Dutch land.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 *landa 为德语 Land 与荷兰语 land 所共享。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *lendh-, meaning land or heath, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的词根被重构为 *lendh-，意为土地或荒地，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: Middle English keeps land for ground and country and begins to use it as a verb for coming ashore.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 land 表示土地与国家，并开始把它用作「上岸」的动词。

items.en: Modern English adds landing, landscape and landlord, and extends the verb to planes and jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 landing、landscape、landlord，并把动词扩展到飞机与工作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on land; the near-meaning group gathers words for ground, country and coming down.
note.cn: 形近组收以 land 构成的词；近义组收表示土地、国家与降落的词。

entries.definition: A person who owns property and rents it to others.

entries.definition: The main mass of land, as opposed to islands.

entries.definition: The solid surface beneath the feet.

entries.definition: The upper layer of earth in which plants grow.

entries.definition: A nation with its own government and territory.
entries.definitionCN: 国家。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake.

normalIntro.en: One short Germanic word covers ground, country and the act of touching down, and its compounds make the connections visible.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短的日耳曼词同时覆盖土地、国家与触地，复合词把这些联系摆了出来。

normal.en: Land is both noun and verb: the land, to land.
normal.cn: land 名动同形：the land 与 to land。

normal.en: Landscape joins land to -scape, a suffix for a view or scene.
normal.cn: landscape 把 land 与表示景色的 -scape 组合。

normal.en: Landlord joins land to lord: the owner of the ground.
normal.cn: landlord 把 land 与 lord 组合，指土地的主人。

normal.en: Landing adds -ing and names both the act and the place where you step down.
normal.cn: landing 加 -ing，既指着陆动作，也指落脚的平台。

normal.en: To land a job keeps the idea of a plane touching down after a search.
normal.cn: land a job 保留飞机经过搜寻后触地的意象。

abstract.en: The same word serves soil, nation and arrival because all three are places where movement stops.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时服务泥土、国家与抵达，因为三者都是运动停下来的地方。

abstract.en: Owning land turns a physical surface into a legal and emotional object.
abstract.cn: 拥有土地把一个物理表面变成为法律与情感的对象。

abstract.en: A landing is a boundary event: above and below meet for a moment.
abstract.cn: landing 是一个边界事件：上与下短暂地相接。

examples.en: After weeks at sea, the sailors finally saw land.
examples.cn: 在海上漂了几周之后，水手们终于看见了陆地。

examples.en: The plane landed safely on the runway.
examples.cn: 飞机安全地降落在跑道上。

examples.en: He landed a good job at a design studio.
examples.cn: 他在一家设计工作室找到了一份好工作。

root: 古英语 land（土地、国土），与德语 Land、荷兰语 land 同源；更深词根 *lendh- 为重构形式，来源不完全确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is solid ground; the senses move from ground to owned soil, to a people's country, then to the act of reaching ground and getting hold of something.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是坚实的地面；义项由地面转到可拥有的土地，再到民族的国土，最后到触地与「弄到手」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey-green coastline appearing ahead of a boat, and a deck finally replaced by soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：船头前方浮出灰绿色的海岸线，甲板终于换成泥土。

branches.en: a strip of shore seen from the deck
branches.cn: 从甲板上望见的一条岸

branches.en: a field divided by low stone walls
branches.cn: 矮石墙分隔的田地

branches.en: a map with a name printed across it
branches.cn: 印着国名的地图

branches.en: wheels meeting the runway
branches.cn: 机轮触到跑道

branches.en: a hand closing on a contract
branches.cn: 手握紧一份合同

intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼词干，靠复合而不是长词缀形成一大族词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: the visible features of an area of land; a picture representing such scenery; the overall pattern of a field of activity; (printing) a page format wider than it is tall
core_image: 从高处望下去，田野、河流与道路拼成一整幅画
scene: 地理课上，老师把投影切成一幅航拍图。The valley landscape was left behind by a retreating glacier.
sceneCN: 这里 landscape 是「地貌景观」（第 1 个义项：一片土地的可见形态）；句意：这条河谷景观是冰川退却后留下的。

senses.title: Visible features of land
senses.definition: the shape, texture, and features of an area of land, including hills, rivers, fields, and vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地的形状、质地与特征，包括山丘、河流、田野与植被
senses.example: Glaciers shaped the landscape of this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川塑造了这条河谷的地貌。
senses.why: Landscape is borrowed from Dutch landschap, land plus -schap, a suffix of state or condition cognate with English -ship. The word began as 'the condition of the land', which is why it can name both a region and how that region looks.
senses.whyCN: landscape 借自荷兰语 landschap，由 land 加 -schap 构成，后者是表示状态或状况的后缀，与英语 -ship 同源。这个词最初意为“土地的状况”，所以它既能命名一片区域，也能命名这片区域的样子。

senses.title: A landscape painting
senses.definition: a painting or photograph whose main subject is natural scenery
senses.definitionCN: 以自然景色为主要题材的绘画或摄影
senses.example: The museum bought a seventeenth-century Dutch landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆买下一幅 17 世纪荷兰风景画。
senses.why: The word entered English in the sixteenth century as an art term: a picture of a land. Dutch painters made the genre famous, and the word travelled with the paintings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 16 世纪作为艺术术语进入英语：一幅关于土地的画。荷兰画家使这一画种闻名，词随画一起传来。

senses.title: Landscape in geography and ecology
senses.titleCN: 地理与生态学中的景观
senses.definition: an area considered as a system of interacting physical, biological, and human features
senses.definitionCN: 被视作物理、生物与人文特征交互系统的区域
senses.example: Landscape ecology studies how patches of habitat connect.
senses.exampleCN: 景观生态学研究栖息地斑块如何连接。
senses.why: Geography turned the word into a technical unit: a landscape is not just a view but a system with boundaries and flows. The visual sense survives inside the scientific one.
senses.whyCN: 地理学把这个词变成技术单位：景观不只是视野，而是有边界与流动的系统。视觉义在科学义内部存活下来。

senses.title: The pattern of a field of activity
senses.definition: the overall arrangement of forces, players, or conditions in a particular area of activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一活动领域中力量、参与者或条件的总体布局
senses.example: The merger changed the competitive landscape of the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并改变了该行业的竞争格局。
senses.why: Twentieth-century business and political writing borrowed the word for a field of play: competitors occupy positions the way hills occupy a view. The metaphor is spatial, and it treats the situation as something seen from above.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的商业与政治写作把这个词借来指一个竞技场：竞争者占据位置，就像山丘占据视野。这个比喻是空间性的，把局势当作从高处看到的东西。

senses.title: Landscape page format
senses.definition: a page or image orientation in which the width is greater than the height
senses.definitionCN: 宽度大于高度的页面或图像方向
senses.example: Print the map in landscape format so the whole route fits.
senses.exampleCN: 把地图打成横向版式，好让整条路线容纳进来。
senses.why: Printing and photography borrowed the word because a wide page resembles a landscape view: the eye moves sideways across it. The term now means orientation alone, with no scenery involved.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与摄影借用这个词，因为宽页面像一幅风景视野：视线横向扫过。这个术语如今只指方向，与景色无关。

senses.title: Landscape design
senses.definition: the planned shaping of gardens, parks, and grounds for use and appearance
senses.definitionCN: 为使用与外观而对花园、公园与场地进行的规划性塑造
senses.example: The landscape of the campus was redesigned last year.
senses.exampleCN: 校园的景观去年被重新设计。
senses.why: Gardening adopted the word in the eighteenth century, when improvers began shaping views rather than merely planting. Landscape became both the object seen and the act of arranging it.
senses.whyCN: 园艺在 18 世纪采用这个词，当时造园者开始塑造视野，而不只是种植。landscape 由此既指被看见的对象，也指安排它的行为。

senses.title: Cultural landscape
senses.definition: a landscape shaped by human activity and carrying the marks of a community's history
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动塑造、带有群体历史印记的景观
senses.example: Rice terraces are a cultural landscape maintained for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 梯田是维护了数百年的文化景观。
senses.why: Heritage studies use the term to reject the split between nature and culture: a landscape is co-produced by people and place. The word then carries a claim about who made what we see.
senses.whyCN: 遗产研究用这个术语来否定自然与文化的截然二分：景观由人与地方共同生产。这个词由此承载一个主张：我们所见的景象是谁造成的。

senses.title: The current overall situation
senses.definition: the general state of affairs that someone surveys before acting
senses.definitionCN: 某人在行动前所审视的总体状况
senses.example: Before launching the product, they studied the regulatory landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 在推出产品之前，他们研究了监管形势。
senses.why: This sense generalises the spatial metaphor to any field: the landscape is what you see when you step back. It implies a survey before a decision, not a detailed analysis of one part.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把空间比喻推广到任何领域：景观是你退后一步看到的东西。它暗示决策前的总体巡视，而不是对某一局部的细致分析。

intro.en: Landscape is a sixteenth-century borrowing from Dutch landschap, land plus -schap (state, condition), cognate with English -ship. It entered English first as a painting term and later spread to geography, gardening, and figurative usage.
intro.cn: landscape 是 16 世纪从荷兰语 landschap 借来的词，由 land 加 -schap（状态、状况）构成，与英语 -ship 同源。它先作为绘画术语进入英语，后来扩展到地理、园艺与比喻用法。

items.en: Dutch landschap combined land with -schap, a suffix of condition or collection, related to English -ship. The word meant 'the condition of the land' or 'a region', not yet a picture.
items.cn: 荷兰语 landschap 把 land 与表示状况或集合的后缀 -schap 结合，后者与英语 -ship 相关。该词意为“土地的状况”或“一片地区”，当时还不是画。

items.en: English borrowed landscape in the sixteenth century as a term for a painting of scenery, alongside the older variant landskip. The artistic sense came first in English usage.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 landscape，作为描绘景色的绘画术语，同时还有较早的变体 landskip。在英语用法中，艺术义最先出现。

items.en: Landscape gardening made the word active: to landscape a park was to arrange its views. The noun and the verb then grew together.
items.cn: 景观造园使这个词变为主动：landscape a park 意为安排它的视野。名词与动词由此一起生长。

items.en: Geography adopted landscape as a technical term for the visible form of a region, studied through maps and fieldwork. Physical and cultural landscapes were distinguished.
items.cn: 地理学采用 landscape 作为区域可见形态的技术术语，通过地图与野外工作研究。自然景观与文化景观被区分开来。

items.en: Business, politics, and journalism extended the word to any field of activity, producing phrases such as 'the competitive landscape'. The spatial metaphor became a standard way to describe strategy.
items.cn: 商业、政治与新闻把这个词扩展到任何活动领域，产生 the competitive landscape 等说法。空间比喻成为描述战略的标准方式。

items.en: Printing and photography borrowed landscape for a page wider than it is tall, because such a page resembles a wide view. The term now names orientation alone.
items.cn: 印刷与摄影借用 landscape 指宽大于高的页面，因为这样的页面像一幅宽视野。这个术语如今只命名方向。

note.en: The look-alike group separates words sharing the -scape suffix or the land element but built on different bases; the near-meaning group separates scenery, terrain, and view.
note.cn: 形近组区分共享 -scape 后缀或 land 成分但基词不同的词；近义组区分 scenery、terrain 与 view。

entries.definition: a view or picture of the sea. It is a modern formation on the model of landscape, replacing land with sea.
entries.definitionCN: 海景或海景画。它是仿 landscape 构成的现代词，把 land 换成 sea。

entries.definition: someone blamed for others' faults. The scape here comes from escape, not from landscape's -schap; the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 替他人受责的人。这里的 scape 来自 escape，而非 landscape 的 -schap；相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: the sliding down of earth or rock, or an overwhelming election victory. It joins land with slide, with no sense of scenery.
entries.definitionCN: 土石滑落，或压倒性的选举胜利。它把 land 与 slide 结合，与景色无关。

entries.definition: the general appearance of a place, especially when attractive. It is uncountable and evaluative; landscape can be neutral and countable.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的整体外观，尤指宜人时。它不可数且带评价；landscape 可中性、可数。

entries.definition: the physical surface of land, especially as it affects movement. It stresses ground conditions, while landscape includes what is seen.
entries.definitionCN: 土地的物理表面，尤指影响行进时。它强调地面条件，而 landscape 包含所见之物。

entries.definition: what can be seen from a particular place. It depends on the observer's position; a landscape exists as a region, whether or not anyone is looking.
entries.definitionCN: 从某一地点能看到的东西。它取决于观察者的位置；landscape 作为区域存在，无论是否有人在看。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: Dutch landschap, the -ship suffix, the painting term of the sixteenth century, and the modern phrase political landscape.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：荷兰语 landschap、-ship 后缀、16 世纪的绘画术语，以及现代说法 political landscape。

normal.en: land + -schap (the same suffix as -ship): landscape is 'the condition of the land'.
normal.cn: land + -schap（与 -ship 同源的后缀）：landscape 就是“土地的状况”。

normal.en: It entered English as a painting word, which is why a landscape can be a picture as well as a place.
normal.cn: 它作为绘画词进入英语，所以 landscape 既可是地方，也可是画。

normal.en: A wide page is printed in landscape because it looks like a wide view.
normal.cn: 宽页面以横向打印，因为它看起来像一幅宽视野。

normal.en: 'Political landscape' treats parties as hills occupying positions in a view.
normal.cn: political landscape 把政党当作占据视野中位置的山丘。

normal.en: seascape and cityscape are modern copies of the same pattern.
normal.cn: seascape 与 cityscape 是同一模式的现代仿造词。

abstract.en: The suffix means condition, not picture: the word is about how land stands, and the picture is a later use.
abstract.cn: 后缀意为状况，而非图画：这个词关乎土地处于何种状态，图画是后来的用法。

abstract.en: Every figurative landscape invites you to step back — the word always implies a viewing distance.
abstract.cn: 每一个比喻性的 landscape 都邀请你退后一步——这个词总暗示一段观看距离。

abstract.en: A cultural landscape denies the split between nature and human history: what you see was co-produced.
abstract.cn: 文化景观否定自然与人类历史的二分：你所见的是共同生产的。

examples.en: The volcanic landscape attracts hikers from around the world.
examples.cn: 这片火山地貌吸引着世界各地的徒步者。

examples.en: The election reshaped the political landscape of the country.
examples.cn: 这次选举重塑了该国的政治格局。

examples.en: The map is printed in landscape so that the coastline fits on one page.
examples.cn: 地图以横向版式印制，好让海岸线容纳在一页内。

dict_mnemonic.text: “兰德斯给普”——荷兰的兰德斯（Land）把土地的样子“给”了出来 → landscape 风景、景观

root: 荷兰语 landschap = land（土地）+ -schap（状态、状况，与英语 -ship 同源）；字面义“土地的状况”，核心是“从远处看到的一片土地的形态与格局”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of landscape all describe a wide arrangement seen as a whole: terrain, a painting, an ecological system, a field of competition, a page, a designed garden, a human-shaped heritage, and the current situation. The word always implies a viewing distance.
sensesIntro.cn: landscape 的八个义项都描述被当作整体看待的宽广布局：地貌、绘画、生态系统、竞争场域、页面、设计的园林、人塑造的遗产，以及当前形势。这个词总暗示一段观看距离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a high vantage point where fields, a river, and roads compose one picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处高处的视点，田野、河流与道路组成一幅画。

branches.en: NATURE: terrain and ecological systems are landscapes as regions, not merely as views.
branches.cn: 自然：地貌与生态系统作为区域性的景观，而不只是视野。

branches.en: ART AND DESIGN: painting and garden-making both arrange what will be seen.
branches.cn: 艺术与设计：绘画与造园都在安排将被看到的东西。

branches.en: SITUATION: fields of activity are surveyed from above and described as layouts.
branches.cn: 形势：活动领域被从高处巡视，并被描述为布局。

branches.en: FORMAT: a wide page borrows the shape of a wide view.
branches.cn: 版式：宽页面借用了宽视野的形状。

branches.en: HERITAGE: a cultural landscape denies the split between nature and human history.
branches.cn: 遗产：文化景观否定自然与人类历史的二分。

intro.en: Landscape is Dutch landschap, land + -schap, cognate with English -ship. The suffix has become productive in English: seascape, cityscape, and moonscape are modern coinages on the same pattern.
intro.cn: landscape 是荷兰语 landschap，由 land + -schap 构成，与英语 -ship 同源。这个后缀在英语中变得能产：seascape、cityscape、moonscape 都是按同一模式造的现代词。

latinIntro.en: Landscape has no Latin root: it is a Germanic compound of land and -schap. The nearest Latin relatives in English vocabulary are terra 'land' and campus 'field', which supply terrain and campus, but they are not etymological relatives.
latinIntro.cn: landscape 没有拉丁词根：它是 land 与 -schap 的日耳曼语复合词。英语词汇中最近的拉丁亲属是 terra“土地”与 campus“田野”，它们提供 terrain 与 campus，但并非词源亲属。

items.meaning: the visible form of a region; a picture of it
items.example: The landscape changed after the flood.

items.meaningCN: 经景观设计的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 酒店有经过设计的园林。

items.meaningCN: 景观布置；造景（-ing 构成名词）
items.exampleCN: 景观布置提升了房产价值。

items.meaningCN: 景观设计师；园林工（-er 表施动者）
items.exampleCN: 景观设计师种下本地草类。

items.meaning: a view or picture of the sea
the visual character of a city
items.example: The cityscape is dominated by glass towers.
items.exampleCN: 城市景观以玻璃塔楼为主。

items.meaningCN: 月球表面景观；荒凉地貌（moon + -scape）
items.example: The mining site resembled a moonscape.
items.exampleCN: 矿区看起来像月球表面。

items.meaning: the solid surface of the earth
items.meaningCN: 土地；陆地（古英语本族词）
items.example: The land rises toward the hills.

items.meaningCN: 风景画（古旧变体，今已罕用）
items.exampleCN: 清单上列有两幅风景画。

definition_zh: 小路；小巷；车道；泳道；航线
definition_en: a narrow road or path; one of the marked strips of a road, track or pool; a fixed route used by ships or aircraft
core_image: 村口一条窄路，两旁是石墙和伸出来的树枝
scene: 雨后的村子很安静，一条窄巷两边的石墙被淋得发亮。She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
sceneCN: 这里是「小路、小巷」（第 1 个义项：狭窄的道路）；句意是她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。图中可辨识物件：石墙、湿路面、树枝。

pos.zh: 小路；小巷；车道；泳道；航线

derivatives.zh: 由 lane 与 way 复合而成，义为「小巷；巷道」
由 multi- 与 lane 复合而成，义为「多车道的」
由 two 与 lane 复合而成，义为「双车道的」

senses.title: A narrow road or path
senses.definition: a narrow road, especially one in the countryside or between buildings
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄的道路，尤指乡间或建筑物之间的小路
senses.example: She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。
senses.why: Old English lane named a narrow path, and narrowness remains the clearest feature of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lane 指狭窄的小路，而「窄」至今仍是这个义项最鲜明的特征。

senses.title: A marked strip of a road
senses.definition: one of the marked strips into which a road is divided for traffic
senses.definitionCN: 道路为车辆行驶而划分出的标线通道之一
senses.example: The truck moved into the left lane to pass the slower car.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车驶入左侧车道，超过那辆开得较慢的车。
senses.why: Once roads were painted and divided, the old word for a narrow path was ready-made for a narrow strip of traffic.
senses.whyCN: 道路画上线并划分之后，原指窄路的旧词正好用来指窄窄的一条车行道。

senses.title: A marked strip of a track or pool
senses.definition: one of the parallel strips used for racing on a track or in a swimming pool
senses.definitionCN: 田径场或游泳池中供比赛使用的平行分道
senses.example: He swam in the outside lane during the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛时他在最外侧的泳道里游。
senses.why: A pool is divided into parallel strips so that swimmers do not collide, and each strip is a narrow path of water.
senses.whyCN: 泳池被分成平行的条带，避免游泳者相互碰撞，而每一条带都是水上的一条窄路。

senses.title: A fixed route for ships or aircraft
senses.definition: a fixed route that ships or aircraft regularly follow
senses.definitionCN: 船只或飞机固定沿用的路线
senses.example: Ships follow a busy lane across the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 船只沿着一条繁忙的航道穿过海峡。
senses.why: A route is also a long narrow strip on a map, so lane extends naturally from a path on land to a path at sea or in the air.
senses.whyCN: 航线在地图上同样是一条狭长的带，所以 lane 从陆上小路自然延伸到海上或空中的路线。

intro.en: Lane is a Germanic word for a narrow path; English has kept the narrowness and applied it to traffic, races and sea routes.
intro.cn: lane 是日耳曼语中指窄路的词；英语保留了「窄」的特征，并把它用到车道、赛道和航线。

items.en: The word is Germanic in origin; a related form is reconstructed, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，可重构出相关形式，但确切形态并不确定。

items.en: Old English lane meant a narrow path or road, often one between hedges or fields.
items.cn: 古英语 lane 指狭窄的小路，常是树篱或田地之间的一条路。

items.en: Middle English kept lane for country paths and for the narrow streets of a town.
items.cn: 中古英语用 lane 指乡间小路和城里的窄街。

items.en: With modern roads and racing, lane was applied to marked strips of traffic, tracks and pools.
items.cn: 随着现代道路与赛事的出现，lane 被用来指标出的车道、跑道和泳道。

items.en: Modern English also uses lane for fixed shipping and air routes.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 lane 指固定的航线和航道。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and one sound-alike; the near-meaning group collects other narrow ways through space.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词和一个同音词；近义组收其他穿越空间的狭窄道路。

entries.definition: The past participle of lie, as in having lain down; it sounds the same but belongs to a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 lie 的过去分词，如「已经躺下」；它与 lane 同音，但属于另一个动词。

entries.definition: A narrow passage or service road, common in Australian and New Zealand English.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄的通道或服务性小路，常见于澳大利亚与新西兰英语。

entries.definition: Tall and thin in an awkward way; only the spelling is close, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦高而显得笨拙的；只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Having several marked strips for traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有数条标线车道的。

entries.definition: A narrow passage between or behind buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之间或后方的一条窄通道。

entries.definition: A track worn by feet or made for walking.
entries.definitionCN: 被人踩出或专为行走而修的小径。

entries.definition: A wide way for vehicles, usually much broader than a lane.
entries.definitionCN: 供车辆行驶的宽阔道路，通常比 lane 宽得多。

entries.definition: A rough path or a prepared course for racing.
entries.definitionCN: 崎岖的小路，或为比赛修整好的跑道。

normalIntro.en: The word stays tied to narrowness; compounds count strips, and the same shape is read on roads, pools and maps.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词始终与「窄」相连；复合词数出条带的数量，而同样的形状在道路、泳池和地图上都能看到。

normal.en: Old English lane meant a narrow path, which is why a country lane is still narrower than a road.
normal.cn: 古英语 lane 指窄路，所以乡间 lane 至今仍比 road 窄。

normal.en: Lain is a homophone but not a relative: it is the past participle of lie, meaning to rest flat.
normal.cn: lain 是同音词而不是同族词：它是 lie 的过去分词，意为平躺。

normal.en: Laneway adds way to lane, and it is the usual word for a narrow service passage in Australasian English.
normal.cn: laneway 在 lane 后加 way，是澳新英语中表示狭窄通道的常用词。

normal.en: Multi-lane and two-lane count the marked strips, so the compound tells you how many streams of traffic there are.
normal.cn: multi-lane 和 two-lane 数的是标线通道，所以复合词直接说明有几股车流。

normal.en: A bus lane is a marked strip reserved for buses, which shows how far lane has moved from a country path.
normal.cn: bus lane 是留给公交车的标线通道，由此可见 lane 已从乡间小路走出多远。

abstract.en: A lane is a line cut through space, whether grass, asphalt or water, and that is why one word serves all of them.
abstract.cn: lane 是在空间里划出的一条线，无论在草地、柏油还是水面上，所以一个词能服务所有这些场景。

abstract.en: Narrowness separates a lane from a road, just as a single track separates one life from another.
abstract.cn: 窄，把 lane 与 road 区分开，就像单条轨迹把一种人生与另一种分开。

abstract.en: Down memory lane shows that a path can also run through time rather than through land.
abstract.cn: down memory lane 说明道路也可以穿过时间，而不只是穿过土地。

examples.en: She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
examples.cn: 她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。

examples.en: The truck moved into the left lane to pass the slower car.
examples.cn: 卡车驶入左侧车道，超过那辆开得较慢的车。

examples.en: He swam in the outside lane during the race.
examples.cn: 比赛时他在最外侧的泳道里游。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「雷恩」——人名雷恩总爱走乡间小路；lane 是小路。

root: 古英语 lane，属日耳曼语固有词，指狭窄的道路；与拉丁语无可靠同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Narrow passage is the core; it widens into traffic strips, racing strips and routes drawn across sea or sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是狭窄的通道；它扩展成车道、赛道，以及画在海面或天空上的航线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow path between two stone walls, just wide enough for one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：两道石墙之间的一条窄路，只容一人走过。

branches.en: a country path with hedges on both sides
branches.cn: 两旁是树篱的乡间小路

branches.en: a town passage too narrow for two carts
branches.cn: 窄得容不下两辆马车的城中通道

branches.en: painted lines splitting a wide road
branches.cn: 把宽路分开的油漆标线

branches.en: ropes floating across a swimming pool
branches.cn: 横在泳池里的浮标绳

branches.en: a dotted route drawn across a chart of the sea
branches.cn: 在海图上画出的一条虚线航线

intro.en: A Germanic noun forms one compound with way, one prefix compound with multi-, and one counting compound with two.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词分别与 way、前缀 multi- 和数词 two 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a narrow road or marked strip
a narrow road in the countryside

definition_zh: 语言；言语；（某一领域的）表达方式；计算机语言
definition_en: a system of spoken or written signs used for communication, or a particular style or code of expression
core_image: 一张围着许多人的旧木桌，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页，几个人正用手势和声音相互回应
scene: 旧木桌旁围坐着来自几座村镇的人，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页。Language was the only tool they had in common that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里指「用于交流的声音与符号系统」（第 1 个义项：人类交流的整体系统）；句意为那天下午，语言是他们唯一共同拥有的工具。可辨识物件：旧木桌、纸页、不同文字、手势。

pos.zh: 语言；言语；表达方式（可数与不可数两用）

derivatives.zh: 语言的；语言学的
语言学
语言学家
多语的
双语的 / 双语者

senses.title: The human system of communication
senses.titleCN: 人类用于交流的符号系统
senses.definition: the shared system of sounds, words and grammar by which people communicate
senses.definitionCN: 人们借以交流的声音、词汇与语法的共享系统
senses.example: Language is learned in company, not from a dictionary alone.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是在与人相处中学到的，而不是只靠词典。
senses.why: the word came from the Latin name for the tongue, so the oldest image is the organ that produces speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语对「舌头」的称呼，因此最古老的画面是发出言语的器官。

senses.title: A particular named tongue
senses.definition: a specific system such as Chinese, Arabic or Swahili, counted as one item
senses.definitionCN: 如汉语、阿拉伯语或斯瓦希里语等具体系统，可作为一个单位计数
senses.example: She speaks four languages and reads two more.
senses.exampleCN: 她会说四种语言，还能读另外两种。
senses.why: once the general capacity was recognized, each separate system needed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 当整体能力被认出之后，每一个独立的系统也需要同一个名称。

senses.title: Speech as it is actually used
senses.definition: the spoken words of a person or group on a given occasion, as opposed to writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体在某一场合说出的具体话语，与书面语相对
senses.example: His language in the meeting was far plainer than his letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上说的话比他的书信朴素得多。
senses.why: the tongue is the instrument of speech, so the word also names the spoken output itself.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是说话的器官，因此这个词也指说出来的产物。

senses.title: The style and wording of a text
senses.definition: the choice of words and sentence patterns that gives a text its tone
senses.definitionCN: 使文本形成某种语气的用词与句式选择
senses.example: The language of the report was careful but cold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的措辞谨慎而冷淡。
senses.why: a text's manner of speech can be described with the same word used for a nation's tongue.
senses.whyCN: 一个文本的说话方式，可以用描述民族语言的同一个词来指称。

senses.title: The vocabulary of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业的行话与术语
senses.definition: the technical words and conventions used by a profession or subject
senses.definitionCN: 某职业或学科使用的术语与惯例
senses.example: Legal language keeps ordinary readers at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 法律行话把普通读者挡在门外。
senses.why: a profession speaks its own tongue, so its terms are called a language.
senses.whyCN: 一个职业说自己的话，因此其术语被称作一种语言。

senses.title: A code for machines
senses.definition: a formal set of instructions that a computer can process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机可以处理的一套形式化指令
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课一次只教一种编程语言。
senses.why: the word was extended to any rule-governed code, including one no human speaks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被扩展到任何有规则的代码，包括没有人说的那种。

senses.title: Non-verbal signals
senses.definition: meaning carried by gesture, posture or tone rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由手势、姿态或语气而非词语承载的意义
senses.example: Her body language said more than her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肢体语言比回答说明了更多。
senses.why: meaning is carried without the tongue at all, and the word follows the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意义完全不经舌头而传递，词也跟着意义走。

senses.title: The human capacity for speech
senses.titleCN: 人类拥有语言的天赋能力
senses.definition: the general human ability to acquire and use a grammar, studied as a faculty
senses.definitionCN: 人类习得并使用语法的总体能力，被当作一种官能来研究
senses.example: Language separates human communication from simple signalling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言使人类交流区别于简单的信号传递。
senses.why: the most abstract sense returns to the original faculty that makes every other sense possible.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的义项回到那项使其他所有义项成为可能的原初官能。

intro.en: Language comes from Old French langage, from Latin lingua 'tongue, language'. The further origin of lingua is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 langage，再上溯拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」。lingua 更早的来源未获证明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant both 'tongue' and 'language'. The sense grew from the organ to what the organ produces, a common pattern in many languages.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」。词义从器官转到器官的产物，这在许多语言中都是常见模式。

items.en: The deeper origin of lingua is unsettled. A link sometimes proposed with a verb meaning 'to lick' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lingua 更深的来源没有定论。有人提出它与一个表「舔」的动词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French langage named speech and the way one speaks; English borrowed it in the age of Norman rule.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语及说话方式；英语在诺曼统治时期借入。

items.en: Middle English used the word for a nation's tongue and for a person's manner of speech, both senses surviving today.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指一个民族的语言，也指个人的说话方式，两义都留存至今。

items.en: Modern technical life extended the word to formal codes, giving programming languages, and to gesture, giving body language.
items.cn: 现代技术生活把词扩展到形式化代码，产生「编程语言」，也扩展到姿态，产生「肢体语言」。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested pre-Latin form of lingua is agreed, and the exact route through French is reconstructed from later records.
items.cn: 来源不确定：lingua 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认书证，经法语传入的确切路径亦由较晚记录构拟。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same root that are often confused; group two holds near neighbours that name communication.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词；第二组是表示交流的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it never names the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，本身不指那套系统。

entries.definition: The scientific study of language, not a language and not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对语言的科学研究，既不是一种语言，也不是一个人。

entries.definition: A person who studies language, or loosely one who knows several.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，或宽泛地指通晓多种语言的人。

entries.definition: An informal word for a foreign language or a jargon; it is playful where language is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指外语或行话的口语说法，语气戏谑，而「语言」一词为中性。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of speaking; it covers sound but not writing or the abstract system.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话的行为或场合，覆盖声音，却不含书面语或抽象系统。

entries.definition: An old word for a language, as in the mother tongue; it is close but archaic in most uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指语言的旧说法，如「母语」；意思接近，但多数用法已古旧。

entries.definition: One variety within a language; calling it a language is a political judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种语言内部的变体；称它为「语言」常是政治判断。

entries.definition: Any system of signs with rules, including machines; it lacks the human and social weight of language.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何有规则的符号系统，包括机器；缺少语言的人类与社会分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'tongue', so the word begins as the body part that makes speech.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词最初就是制造言语的身体部位。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: foreign language, body language, programming language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：外语、肢体语言、编程语言。

normal.en: The adjective, the discipline and the person all come from the same root.
normal.cn: 形容词、学科与人都出自同一词根。

normal.en: The family runs linguistic, linguistics, linguist, multilingual, bilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言的」「语言学」「语言学家」「多语的」「双语的」。

normal.en: Counting languages uses the plural, speaking in general uses the singular.
normal.cn: 数具体语言用复数，泛指说话能力用单数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every sheet is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每张纸都出自不同的笔迹。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built from sounds rather than stones.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用声音而非石头搭成的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens a different door for every listener.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙，对每个听者打开不同的一扇门。

examples.en: Language changes faster in cities than in isolated valleys.
examples.cn: 语言在城市里的变化比在封闭山谷中更快。

examples.en: The two communities share a border but not a language.
examples.cn: 这两个社群共享一条边界，却不共享一种语言。

examples.en: Nurses are trained to read the body language of anxious patients.
examples.cn: 护士受过训练，能读懂焦虑病人的肢体语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兰格维吉」——拦住陌生人开口，靠的就是这套声音与符号的系统。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 进入英语；词义由器官转向器官的产物。lingua 更深来源不确定，与表「舔」动词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one organ: the tongue produces speech, speech becomes a named system, that system takes styles and jargons, and the same word is finally lent to machines and to silent gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个器官铺开：舌头产生言语，言语成为具名的系统，系统又生出风格与行话，最后同一个词被借给机器与无声的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table, many scripts, and hands answering in gesture and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子、多种文字，人们用手势与声音相互回应。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: the human faculty and its shared system are the two sides of one coin.
branches.cn: 能力：人类的官能与共享系统是同一枚硬币的两面。

branches.en: COUNTED TONGUES: each separate system can be named and counted.
branches.cn: 可数的语言：每一套独立系统都可被命名与计数。

branches.en: BEYOND WORDS: actual speech and silent gesture both carry meaning.
branches.cn: 超出词语：实际说出的话与无声的姿态都承载意义。

branches.en: TONE OF A TEXT: word choice alone can make writing warm or cold.
branches.cn: 文本的语气：仅靠选词就能让文字变暖或变冷。

branches.en: RULED CODES: a profession's jargon and a machine's instructions are both governed sets.
branches.cn: 有规则的代码：专业行话与机器指令都是受规则支配的集合。

intro.en: The word is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin root meaning 'tongue', and that root also builds the whole linguistic family.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语成形的名词，建在拉丁语表「舌头」的词根上，这个词根也构成整个「语言」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, linguist and linguistics through French and Latin endings; the same root appears in the adjective for 'tongue-shaped'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 经法语与拉丁词尾衍生出「语言」「语言学家」与「语言学」；同一词根也出现在表「舌形」的形容词里。

items.meaning: the organ of speech, and speech itself
items.example: The root already carries both the body part and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根已同时带着器官与其产物。

items.example: Language is older than any dictionary.
items.exampleCN: 语言比任何词典都古老。

items.example: The linguist recorded the last speakers.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家记录了最后的说话者。
语言证据为这份文本定了年代。
语言学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: Bilingual signs appeared at the airport.

items.exampleCN: 这座城市以多语并存为荣。

items.example: The manual is full of technical lingo.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册满是技术行话。
